findings: Codex cross-provider review for AO-MA-823 agrees with the corrected design: the workflow delegates ADR-0005 changelog discipline to the canonical `ao-kernel quality check-changelog` CLI instead of reimplementing decision logic in YAML.

The workflow uses the current CLI signature (`--base-changelog`, `--head-changelog`, `--out`, repeated `--diff-path`, and optional `--chore-no-changelog` / `--chore-rationale`). The previous outdated `--base` / `--labels-json` shape is not used.
The PR now includes a real `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` entry for the new CI enforcement lane, so the newly introduced workflow passes without requiring a `chore-no-changelog` label bypass.

Security posture remains narrow: pull_request event only, contents:read and pull-requests:read, persist-credentials:false, no secrets context, no admin token, no branch-protection/ruleset/CODEOWNERS mutation, and all guard flags remain false.

Scope-reviewed binding is current-PR exact: the changed_files list matches the sorted `git diff --name-only origin/main` output, including the changelog entry, workflow, shape test, and review-evidence artifacts.

E-1-4 pre-commit hook invariant was narrowed to its own hook write-set: workflow mutations now fail only when the E-1-4 hook slice is active, while E-1-3 workflow PRs are governed by their own changelog-enforcement workflow shape tests.
